label: Animals at the Tower Menagerie
name: Animals at the Tower Menagerie
src_text_orig: Endlich sahen wir die Löwen. Deren sind sehr viele, davon Einige auß Indien geschikt, andre hier geboren sind. Der alte Löwe ist sehr groß, haaricht und macht eine ernsthaffte mine. Er hat eine Löwin bey ihm. Sein nachbar aber schläft bey einem kleinen Hunde. Zwey Leoparden sind da die ungemein schön geflekt sind. Drey Tieger, davon der eine fast keine fleken hat und übern stok springt wie eine kaze, der dritte aber sehr schön geflekt ist. Sie nehren auch einige Adlers, die braun sind, nicht eben ungemein groß und sehr scharf schreyen. Eine fremde raze sieht auch eine Tiegerkaze aus, das zwey artige Thiere sind. Die Preise sind alle reglirt: Die Löwen 1 shilling, die Krone 18 pence, dem Jeoman 2 shilling, im Zeughauß 5 pence und bey den Harnischen 6 pence. Damit gingen wir in der Taverne speisen. Schlecht und malpropre.
src_text_translation: Finally we saw the lions. There are a lot of them, some of them from India, others born here. The old lion is very big, hairy and makes a serious face. He has a lioness with him. But his neighbour sleeps with a small dog. There are two leopards, which are extremely beautifully spotted. Three tigers, one of which has almost no spots and jumps over a stick like a cat, but the third is very beautifully spotted [sic]. They also feed some eagles, which are brown, not particularly large and scream very sharply. A foreign breed that looks like a tiger-cat, of which there are two animals. The prices are all regulated: the lions 1 shilling, the crown 18 pence, the Yeoman 2 shillings, in the arsenal 5 pence and with the armoury 6 pence. We then went to dine in the tavern. Bad and filthy.
src_source:
Haller, Albrecht von. Albrecht Hallers Tagebuch seiner Studienreise nach London, Paris, Strassburg und Basel, 1727-1728. Edited by Erich Hintzsche, Hans Huber, 1968, p. 17.

There are two manuscripts documenting Haller’s travels, N Haller 39 and N Haller 38. Both are located at the Burgerbibliothek Bern but have not been digitalized. N Haller 38 are his original notes in tiny handwriting, with barely any space, and many crossed out sections, making it very hard to read. N Haller 39 was written after the completion of his travels, based on his notes, but giving a much more detailed account. The editor, Erich Hintzsche, transcribed both of these versions: the notes (N Haller 38) are Albrecht Hallers Tagebuch seiner Studienreise nach London, Paris, Straßburg und Basel, 1727-1728, published in 1968, and the extended version (N Haller 39) is Albrecht Hallers Tagebücher seiner Reisen nach Deutschland, Holland und England, 1723-1727, published in 1971. We are quoting from both versions, so be aware which one is cited.
